How the methods work (animated)

Source: vignettes/articles/concepts.Rmd
concepts.Rmd

Short animations for the ideas behind MosaiClusteR. Each is a small vector graphic that loops, so it stays crisp at any size. Teal and amber mark two sources; blue and navy mark objects and results.

Integration paradigms

The five ways MosaiClusteR combines sources.

Direct integration

The sources are concatenated into one wide matrix and clustered once. Fast and transparent (ADC, ADEC).

Similarity fusion

Each source gives an object-by-object similarity network. The networks reinforce each other through cross-diffusion and converge to one fused network (SNF).

Voting consensus

Many partitions vote on whether each pair of objects belongs together. The votes accumulate into a consensus that is then clustered (M_ABC, CEC, EvidenceAccumulation).

Hierarchy

Per-source hierarchies are consensed into a single dendrogram, read from the leaves up to the root (HierarchicalEnsembleClustering, EHC).

Inside the algorithms

A closer look at two mechanisms that recur across the methods.

Feature bundling (the ABC family)

For each source, M-ABC repeatedly draws a weighted subsample of features (a “bundle”), clusters on it, and records the result. Signal that hides in a subset of features is found across many bundles.

Consensus co-association

Every base clustering casts a vote for each pair of objects. The votes build an object-by-object co-association matrix, and its block structure is the consensus the final clustering recovers.

Choosing and checking the clusters

How many clusters are there? The average silhouette width rises to a peak at the number of clusters the data supports.

Data nuggets

For very large samples, the objects are first compressed into a few weighted representatives (nuggets). Feature weighting and clustering then run on the small set.

For the full method details, see the method comparison and the guides.
